requirement: Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation.
rationale:
`read_node.fn` says criterion code uses `ValidationContext.read` for reading a node. The only testable obligation is that this operation exists with the specified shape: `read(&self, &NodeId) -> Result<NodeContent, Error>`, and that it reads a node and records the fingerprint of the returned contents. The detailed recording semantics belong to the cited `ValidationContext.read` and `read_node.inputs`. I did not reassess those.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It calls `inspection.read(&1)` directly on a `ValidationContext`, which pins the signature and the Result return type. It covers two inputs: an empty string and a large multi-byte Unicode string. For both it asserts that:
- `contents.format()` equals the original content.
- The returned contents stay unchanged after the graph is later modified.
- `inspection.dependencies()` holds a `Dependency::Node(1, fp(original))` entry, so the fingerprint was recorded.
- The recorded read count is `[1, 1]`.
- The finished record is no longer current once the contents change.

The test also covers the failure path. `failed.read(&9)` returns `Err("missing")` and leaves `failed.dependencies()` empty, so a failed read records nothing.

Because the subject only requires use of this operation, one marked test that calls `read` directly and asserts its returned value, recorded fingerprint and error behavior is adequate. I found no untested obligation or assertion gap.
